clue.text: Considering call about revised grade

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, so the call wraps the reworked letters

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them

indicators.note: something revised has been altered, so the letters of grade are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks over a phone call about a grade that has been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' marks the anagram of the grade letters, and 'about' wraps the call word round them; 'Considering' is used as a preposition, as in 'considering the weather'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, regarding means concerning or with respect to, the same as considering in 'considering the cost'.

clue.text: You have one second to leave without pudding

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the leave word goes round the second

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon
S is the abbreviation for second, one of them

explanation.surface: Someone is told they have a second to go and will miss the sweet course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: S goes inside DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the British word for the sweet course that ends a meal, also called dessert.

clue.text: So coveted new shelter for birds

indicators.note: new signals the letters of so coveted are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A much-wanted fresh home for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovecote is a small house or box built to hold pigeons or doves.

clue.text: Remote possibility given by rotten card in monopoly

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
Chance is one of the two piles of cards drawn in the board game Monopoly

explanation.surface: A slim prospect comes from a bad card drawn in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is the property-trading board game whose squares send players to draw Chance or Community Chest cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An off chance is a slight likelihood that something may happen.

clue.text: Monstrous woman's back. Therefore take steps round the edge

indicators.note: back means the word for therefore is read from its end to its start

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first and last letters, here of steps

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman returns, so she walks around the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' marks the reversal of the Latin for therefore; 'round the edge' takes the first and last letters of 'steps'. The apostrophe-s is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female giant in fairy tales who eats people, a monstrous woman.

clue.text: Dark-grey compound of carbon, hydrogen, argon, cobalt and aluminium

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon
Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A chemistry list describing a dark substance made of several elements.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a formula, and charcoal is indeed mostly carbon, but the definition is the colour at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal names a very dark shade of grey, after the burnt wood.

clue.text: It's as if Ghana made new language

indicators.note: made new signals that the letters of if Ghana are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a West African country inventing a fresh tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghani is a name sometimes used for the speech of Afghanistan, chiefly Pashto.

clue.text: Fib after cleaner finds cocaine

indicators.note: after places the fib piece behind the cleaner piece

parts.note: a char, short for charwoman, is a British word for a cleaner
a fib is a small lie

explanation.surface: A cleaner turns up drugs and tells a lie about it.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR, a charwoman, is an old British word for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is slang for the drug, from the C of its name.

clue.text: There's some cockerel on grill soon

indicators.note: some means only part of the words cockerel on grill is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A barbecue will soon have chicken on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erelong is an old word meaning before long, shortly.

clue.text: He suspends word game

explanation.definitionFit: An executioner is someone who hangs people; it is also the pencil game of guessing letters before a gallows is drawn.

clue.text: Gold trees swaying on plain

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: swaying trees move about, so the letters of trees are shuffled

explanation.surface: Golden trees sway in the wind on open flat land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swaying' turns TREES into STERE. 'plain' looks like a noun for flat land, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and unadorned, the same as plain in style.

clue.text: Select cap to wear for pageant

indicators.note: something worn is altered from its first state, so select cap is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a hat to wear to a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a grand public show, as a pageant is.

clue.text: Being thoughtful, I have swans at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the swans piece before the I have piece

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: Someone lost in thought notices swans leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is the female swan, the male being a cob.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensive means deep in thought, reflective.

clue.text: Sleepy partygoer in the large bedroom by the river

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a large shared bedroom
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A drowsy reveller lies in a dormitory beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The partygoer is the dozy guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland. The Ouse is a river in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The rodent famous for hibernating is the sleepy guest at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: Up on the rocks, a siren can make it

indicators.note: on the rocks means wrecked, so the letters of a siren are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A siren on the rocks can lure sailors up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sirens sang from rocks to wreck sailors, so 'on the rocks' sits naturally in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has arisen has got up, so the word means up, out of bed.

clue.text: Passing on event?

parts.note: passing on suggests death, but here it is handing a baton to the next runner in a team race

explanation.definitionFit: In this team race each runner passes a baton to the next, so it is an event built on passing on.

clue.text: Bridge players take an instant to read bulletin

parts.note: in the card game bridge the four players are North, East, West and South
a flash is an instant, as in 'in a flash'

explanation.surface: Card players pause briefly to read the latest bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit at the four compass points, so the letters N, E, W, S are crossword shorthand for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a short urgent news report, a bulletin.

clue.text: Record one's let out in letter

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
one is I in Roman numerals, so one's gives I'S

indicators.note: out signals the letters of let are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A record releases one person's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the epistles of the New Testament.

clue.text: Liking for writer's song

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool, a writer
a chant is a simple sung tune

explanation.surface: A preference for a songwriter's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong fondness or taste for something.

clue.text: Agrees to see new musical

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of agrees are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone consents to go to a fresh stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is a stage and film musical about 1950s high-school life.

clue.text: Entering street in France, head of Eurostar can see train

indicators.note: entering means the following pieces go inside the street word

parts.note: rue is the French for street

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Eurostar

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: In a French street, the boss of the cross-Channel rail firm watches a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the Eurostar, but it means a group of followers. Eurostar is the train service through the Channel Tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants following an important person, a train in the old sense.

clue.text: One hundred euros up front — that's solvent!

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
a ton is slang for a hundred
E is the abbreviation for euros

explanation.surface: Paying a hundred euros in advance shows someone has money to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' looks like an adjective for having money, but it is the noun, a liquid that dissolves things.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a liquid used to dissolve other substances, as in nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: A sapper in new tower

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the new word

parts.note: mint means brand new, as in mint condition
RE, the Royal Engineers, is the corps of sappers

explanation.surface: A military engineer is inside a recently built tower.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque.

clue.text: Unpredictable occurrences from confused ram, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the pieces and take what they sound like

parts.note: someone vague is confused or unclear; Aries, the first sign of the zodiac, is the ram

explanation.surface: Odd happenings stem from a muddled male sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for VAGUE ARIES spoken aloud; the match is loose, as Aries stresses its first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are erratic changes or whims, things that happen without warning.

clue.text: A right rascal seen at European shops

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rascal

explanation.surface: A real scoundrel is spotted at shops on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered passage lined with shops.

clue.text: Polish device for carrying the sick

definitions.text: Polish device for carrying the sick

parts.words: Polish device for carrying the sick
parts.note: Polish suggests something from Poland, but read as pole-ish it describes a carrier built on two poles for moving patients

explanation.surface: A piece of medical kit made in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Polish' as 'pole-ish': the thing has two long poles with canvas between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a frame of two poles with fabric between, used to carry injured people.

clue.text: Shorten dog at the front and the back

indicators.note: at the front places the dog piece before the back piece

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a tail is the back end of something

explanation.surface: Someone trims a dog both front and rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short or reduce.

clue.text: African articles about western diary

indicators.note: about means the article pair goes round the reversed diary

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a second an, the clue's articles being plural

indicators.note: in an across clue western means read leftwards, towards the west

parts.note: a log is a daily record, a diary

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces about a cowboy's journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' marks a reversal, as across entries read west to east; 'about' puts the turned diary word between two copies of the article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Angola is a country in southern Africa, so someone from there is African.

clue.text: Noble lady starts to dust uncle's board game

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each of the next words is taken

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A titled woman begins to clean her uncle's games board.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is the wife of a duke or a woman holding a duke's rank.

clue.text: Small meeting of heads in Paris about opening of academy

indicators.note: about means the two heads go round the opening letter

parts.note: tete is French for head
a second tete, the clue's heads being plural

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of academy

explanation.surface: Senior figures in Paris gather to discuss founding an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: TETE is French for head; two of them sit round the A of academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, literally head to head.
